items.claim: Prov.15.26 is correctly kept single_proverb; the tocevat-YHWH echo to 15:8-9 is real but non-adjacent and rightly disclosed only as texture, not a cluster driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.15.26 תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת רָ֑ע repeats the construct phrase at oshb:Prov.15.8/15.9 (תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה / תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה), but the immediate neighbors oshb:Prov.15.25 and oshb:Prov.15.27 share no content token with 15:26 beyond the bare divine name; the sixteen-verse intervening gap (15:10-15:25) between 15:9 and 15:26 is confirmed by direct count. sweep.py --skel "toevat YHWH" (contiguous skeleton, cross-checked verse-by-verse to exclude false hits) returns the construct phrase at 11 verses book-wide (3:32, 11:1, 11:20, 12:22, 15:8, 15:9, 15:26, 16:5, 17:15, 20:10, 20:23), none consecutive with 15:26, so the row's non-adjacency claim and single_proverb default both hold.

items.claim: The 15:31-33 proverb_cluster rests on a genuine byte-grounded two-link catchword chain (tokhachat 31-32, musar 32-33), and the disclosed 15:30 echo is correctly excluded as a weaker root-only, different-skeleton match.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms byte tier for oshb:Prov.15.31 תּוֹכַ֣חַת and oshb:Prov.15.32 תּ֝וֹכַ֗חַת, each governed by a participle of the shama root (שֹׁ֭מַעַת / וְשׁוֹמֵ֥עַ); oshb:Prov.15.32 מ֭וּסָר (absolute) and oshb:Prov.15.33 מוּסַ֣ר (construct) likewise byte-match. The disclosed oshb:Prov.15.30 שְׁמוּעָ֥ה shares only the shama root, not the skeleton token, with 15:31's שֹׁ֭מַעַת (a noun 'report' vs. a feminine participle 'hearing', on an unrelated topic), so it correctly fails prov_device_inventory.json's catchword_adjacency bar (skeleton-tier, stoplist-filtered shared-token pairs) and is rightly excluded from the chain even though it stands in the verse immediately before it.

items.claim: 16:2 is correctly kept single_proverb; beyond the bare divine name, 16:1 and 16:2 share no content token.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.1 (לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי לֵ֑ב ... מַעֲנֵ֥ה לָשֽׁוֹן) and oshb:Prov.16.2 (כָּֽל דַּרְכֵי אִ֭ישׁ זַ֣ךְ בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן רוּח֣וֹת יְהוָֽה) share only the bare divine-name token (יְהוָֽה); 'adam' (16:1) and 'ish' (16:2) are different lexemes for 'man', and לֵ֑ב (heart, 16:1) has no counterpart in 16:2, confirming the rejected 16:1-join correctly.

items.claim: 16:3's imperative-plus-result reading is grammatically accurate, and its rejection of a 16:2 join (no shared token beyond the divine name) is byte-confirmed.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.3 opens with the 2ms imperative גֹּ֣ל (root gll), a verb form with no counterpart in 16:2's verbless clause. The row's disclosed non-adjacent echo of מַחְשְׁבֹתֶֽיךָ (16:3) to מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת at oshb:Prov.15.22 is a genuine shared root (chshb), fourteen verses back (15:23-16:2 intervening), correctly disclosed as texture only and not claimed as a cluster driver.

items.claim: 16:4's declarative/concessive reading and its rejection of a 16:3 join are both accurate; no content token beyond the divine name is shared with either neighbor.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.4's וְגַם is additive/concessive (no adversative particle in the verse), matching the row's 'extends rather than opposes' reading. כֹּ֤ל (16:4, 'all') and גֹּ֣ל (16:3, imperative 'commit') are superficially similar strings but different roots (kll vs gll); the row does not claim them as a shared token, correctly.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative rebuts only a weak 'gap-free YHWH-token run' rival and omits the strongest real rival: a byte-verified lev/adam inclusio bracketing the very 15:33-16:9 span the row discusses.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.1 opens לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי לֵ֑ב ('to man...heart') and oshb:Prov.16.9 opens לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם ('heart of man') -- the same two content words, lev and adam, recur in inverted order at the two boundary verses of the 15:33-16:9 span, a chiastic envelope the row never engages (collate.py confirms byte tier on both quoted strings). book_strategy/Prov.md section 6 itself names 'the 15:33-16:9 YHWH cluster' as an owner-ratified example of the cohesion-evidence class needed for a proverb_cluster row, so the un-rebutted rival is the strategy's own named candidate, not a strawman; the row instead defeats only the weaker 16:8 divine-name-gap argument. This does not by itself require re-clustering: the interior verses (16:2-16:7) still show no pairwise content-token overlap beyond the divine name, so single_proverb likely still holds for 16:5. But as written the rejected_alternative fails the strongest-rival test.

items.claim: The claimed distance between 16:6's yirat-YHWH phrase and 15:33's is arithmetically wrong: it is six verses later, not seven.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.15.33 יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה and oshb:Prov.16.6 וּבְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה byte-match the same construct phrase (collate.py byte tier). Counting the verses from 15:33 to 16:6 (16:1, 16:2, 16:3, 16:4, 16:5, 16:6) gives a six-verse span, not seven as the row states. The phrase-echo itself and its 'texture, not driver' treatment are otherwise correct and consistent with the row's own single_proverb call.

items.claim: 16:7's conditional/synthetic reading is accurate and its darkhe-ish echo to 16:2 is a genuine non-adjacent shared bigram, correctly kept as texture rather than a cluster driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.7 בִּרְצ֣וֹת יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי אִ֑ישׁ shares the exact bigram דַּרְכֵי אִ֑ישׁ with oshb:Prov.16.2's כָּֽל דַּרְכֵי אִ֭ישׁ, four verses apart (16:3-16:6 intervening). 16:6 and 16:7 share no content token beyond the divine name, confirming the rejected 16:6 join; גַּם is additive ('even'), with no adversative particle in the verse, matching the row's synthetic/conditional device_notes reading.
